thesis.claim: How agents die decides who is left to play. In B2, with at least 30% of an agent's tokens kept at home, fewer than half the agents hold a single token after iteration 300; with only the last token kept, more than two in three do; with nothing kept, worlds starve: at least half fall below 100 agents within 1,000 iterations.
thesis.why: An agent that cannot lose its last token can stake everything else on one neighbour at no risk to itself, and brains that see do: in a pilot with only the last token kept, 75% of the agents held exactly one token at iteration 1,500, against 1% in the baseline's blind world. Kept to 30% of its tokens, an agent's stake stays spread: 35–61% at one token in pilots. With nothing kept, agents stake themselves to death and worlds starved to a single agent within 300 iterations in both pilot seeds.
thesis.confirm: Median over iterations 300 to 1,000 of the share of agents holding one token (from the frames): below 0.5 in at least 7 of the 10 B2 worlds, above 0.67 in at least 7 of the 10 worlds with keep_home 0.01; and at least 5 of the 10 worlds with keep_home 0 have fewer than 100 agents after some game.
thesis.refute: Any of the three fails: the share at one token does not follow what is kept at home, or worlds without it do not starve.
